records.note: Compound claim about therapists on insurance-based platforms: they 'are going to quit', 'go back to doing less scalable work', and 'everyone's gonna be worse off'. No countable set (which therapists, which platforms, how many), no series and no threshold can be written from the text; 'everyone's gonna be worse off' is a slogan. A third party (therapists) decides and the forecaster holds no role in a named entity, so CONTROL does not apply. No horizon words.

'A fine strategy for a company until it's not' names no company, no event and no benchmark; the sentence is close to a tautology (a strategy works until it stops working). No entity, observable event, series or threshold can be written without inventing one, and no horizon words are given.

Evaluation of a proposed intervention in the conditional mood: payment-systems training 'could help' clinicians and 'would not address' friction and low reimbursement. No future state is asserted about the world (no claim that such training will be offered or adopted), and the effects named ('help clinicians navigate', 'frustrations') have no observable criterion, so VAGUE would also apply.

'Insurance providers must offer solutions' is a prescription ('must') with no predictive reading in the sentence. The finder's conditional reading (clinicians will not return to insurance networks without such solutions) would need a countable set of clinicians, a series and a period that the text does not give, so it would fail as VAGUE in any case.

Proposed solution described in the conditional mood: enforcement of parity and prompt-payment laws 'would make' payers' adversarial attitude 'less hazard free'. The author does not claim enforcement will occur, and the consequent has no observable criterion (no enforcement action, penalty or count is named), so no conditional event can be written. VAGUE would also apply.

Description of how a value-based, shared-risk model 'would' behave (clinicians rewarded for keeping patients out of hospital, aligned goals, less incentive to block payments). It explains a model rather than asserting that any payer, program or state will adopt it; no adopting body, program, date or measurable effect is given. VAGUE would also apply.

'The opportunity ... to go at risk ... is coming' names no payer, program, contract, state or series, so no coverage_decision or quantity event can be written without inventing the deciding body. 'Is coming' is a bin A phrase but not a deadline (anchors.json). The finder's CONTROL reading (the at-risk model of the author's own companies) is noted but not needed: the statement fails first for lack of an observable event.

'We see a shift towards shared-risk, value-based care' is a present-tense perception of a trend. Read forward, it has no metric, threshold, series, payer or period, so no quantity_threshold event can be written without inventing a benchmark. No horizon words.

Generic closing claim of a survey write-up: continued study 'will further highlight these issues and lead to improvement in mental health care'. 'Improvement in mental health care' has no benchmark, metric or deciding body; 'highlight these issues' is not an observable event. Also outside the five areas (research activity), so OUT_OF_AREA would apply as well.

Restates the Solutions-section model in the conditional mood: value-based care 'would assist in reducing' contentious relations between providers and insurers. Conditional on an adoption the author does not predict, with a consequent ('less contentious relations') that has no observable criterion. VAGUE would also apply. Same reading as owen-1478.

Characterization of the incoming administration as 'even more anti-trans than Texas alone': a comparative with no benchmark and no observable event (no rule, order, agency action or law is named). 'On the eve of new administration' dates the statement, not an outcome. No event can be written without inventing the policy action to be measured.

'To do otherwise is a catastrophe when it comes to civil litigation' is a slogan: no case, court, defendant, count or amount can be written from the text. The 2025 introduction restates the thesis of the 2022 article as a warning, not as a dated expectation; no horizon words.

Claim that plaintiffs with legal standing for a malpractice suit would be easy to find ('should not be a needle in a haystack'). Ease of finding plaintiffs is not an observable event; no suit, court or docket is named, and the sentence is attached to advice to the ACLU. Text from the 2022 body republished on the statement date given in the packet (2025-01-05).

'Almost unfathomable medico-legal liability' for Texas Children's Hospital names no suit, claim, judgment or amount; liability exposure is not an observable event and the intensifier is a slogan. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05. No horizon words.

'Imminent collapse' of the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services: 'collapse' has no criterion in the text (abolition, mass resignation, court order, loss of funding), so writing one would invent it. 'Imminent' is not a deadline per anchors.json. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05; SATIRE (hyperbole) would also apply.

'Could lead to a möbius loop of iterative reports of failures to protect kids' describes a paradox inside DFPS self-reporting. No count, series, threshold or deciding body can be written; 'reports' is not a defined observable set. The hedge 'could' would be bin C if the statement were admitted. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

Expectation of DFPS staff attrition ('a poor employee retention plan ... I would imagine'). No threshold, series, period or benchmark for attrition is given, so no quantity_threshold event can be written. Also outside the five areas (state agency staffing). Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

Hypothetical scenario about an unnamed, invented Texas telehealth child psychiatrist: 'if sued, she can and should lose' and her insurer 'would have to pay out'. No real party, case, court or docket exists to name, so no court_outcome event can be written. A thought experiment, so NOT_FORECAST would also apply. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

Compound claim: 'medical malpractice lawsuits' and 'doctors fleeing your state' follow 'pretty quickly' from Abbott's order. Neither part has a countable set (no defendant, docket or count; no physician series or threshold), and 'pretty quickly' is not a deadline. Both parts fail on the same test, so the record is not split. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

'Opens the door for definitive enforcement of the fiduciary rule' does not assert that any enforcement action will occur; it states a possibility with no enforcing body, case, plan or date. 'ERISA plan insufficiencies that are clear and unambiguous' is an assessment, not an event. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

'How unbelievably easy it would be to make a claim against a Texas employer' is a judgment about the ease of a hypothetical claim, not an observable event; no claim, plaintiff, plan or court is named. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

'All of them will go to jail if they do so': 'all' quantifies a set the author himself puts at zero (Texas providers of gender-affirming care to trans youth), so there is no countable set; no court, prosecution or case is named. Evident hyperbole inside a rhetorical Q&A, so SATIRE would also apply; VAGUE holds under a literal reading and does not depend on tone. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

'Causes every Texas employer ... and every Texas insurance plan ... A Serious Problem' is a slogan: 'A Serious Problem' has no observable criterion (no enforcement action, penalty, suit or count), and 'every' quantifies a set with no resolution source. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

'Lawsuits that are just going to totally crush noncompliant plans': no plan, suit, court or outcome criterion (judgment, settlement, amount) is named, so 'totally crush' cannot be resolved. The suits would be filed at the author's own initiative ('have a ERISA attorney file lawsuits'), so the antecedent is CONTROL as well. Text from the 2022 body republished on 2025-01-05.

'More hope is coming, too' is a slogan inside an event promotion: no treatment, regulator, trial or series is named, and 'more' has no countable set. 'Is coming' is not a deadline. The event promoted (RAMHT) is the author's own.

'These treatments can change the landscape of reimbursement and risk management' is a capability slogan with no payer, policy, code or series; 'payers need to know' is normative framing (NORMATIVE would also apply). No observable event can be written.

Lineup of the author's own event (RAMHT SF 2025, 12 January 2025; the author is the RAMHT organizer per the affiliations list), naming his own organizations Fermata, Acacia Clinics and Videra Health among the participants. Own-event programming, not a third-party decision. Also outside the five areas.

Attendance at the author's own event (RAMHT SF 2025): Radial (the author is its Chief Medical Officer) 'might be skulking around' and iRxReminder staff 'will be hanging out'. Own-event logistics involving organizations in the affiliations list, not a third-party decision. The iRxReminder part is relayed 'on good authority' about another organization's action seven days ahead, so REPORT would also apply; also outside the five areas.
'We are bringing live demos' announces programming of the author's own event (RAMHT SF 2025). The forecaster's own organization makes it happen by its own decision. Also outside the five areas.

'MDHub.ai will be at RAMHT SF 2025' is an attendance announcement for the author's own event six days ahead; the lineup is under the organizer's control. REPORT (another organization's action 30 days or less ahead) and OUT_OF_AREA would also apply.

'There may be some subsequent trademark issues' between the author's clinic Fermata and an agtech company of the same name. 'Trademark issues' has no observable criterion (a demand letter, a USPTO opposition, a suit, a rename), so no event can be written without inventing it; 'subsequent' is not a deadline. The author's own company could initiate any such action, so CONTROL would also apply. Sincere line inside an otherwise satirical post.

'We may have to include Health in the name' is the author's own company's naming decision (Fermata; the author is co-founder per the affiliations list). The outcome is made by the forecaster's organization by its own decision.
'Tomorrow, I will write more about health' is the author's own publishing plan for his newsletter. Own action, not a third-party decision; also outside the five areas.

'Humans have tamed many forces in the natural world; it's easy to imagine we will continue to do so' concerns no regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome. It is also a truism with no observable event, threshold or deadline, so VAGUE would apply as well.

'I don't think they're gonna give it up without a fight': 'Big Health companies' is an undefined set (UnitedHealth Group is only the example), 'give it up' names no scope (which prior-authorization requirements, for which services), and 'without a fight' cannot be resolved even if prior authorization were withdrawn. No horizon words. If admitted, the denial phrase 'I don't think ... gonna' would be bin B with asserts false.

Conditional on the author's own hypothetical proposal (every prior-authorization request delivered in person by a licensed payer physician), which no body has proposed to enact and which is not an observable event. The consequent, insurers 'would run out of physicians willing' to do it, has no threshold, series or period. No conditional event can be written.

'Tonight, we kick off the JPM Health conference in SF' refers to the author's own event (RAMHT SF 2025, 12 January 2025) opening JPM week. Own-event logistics, not a third-party decision; also outside the five areas.

'A lot of people will want to get into a psilocybin trial' generalizes from one published trial's applicant count. 'A lot of people' has no threshold, no named future trial and no series (applications, screening numbers), so no quantity_threshold event can be written without inventing all three. No horizon words.

'But that's for another substack post' is a content promise about the author's own newsletter. Own action, not a third-party decision; also outside the five areas. The article is a re-run, so the promise may date from the original version.

Compound claim that next-generation ADHD treatments (TMS, the Monarch eTNS device, LSD derivatives sponsored by Mind Medicine) 'promise better efficacy and a lower side effect profile'. Both parts are comparatives with no benchmark (better than what, on which endpoint, in which trial), and 'the next generation of treatments' is a set with no resolution source, so no trial_result event can be written without inventing the trial and endpoint. Both parts fail on the same test, so the record is not split. The author discloses a MindMed shareholding in footnote 9; recorded here because the record is rejected.
